Chapter Eight. The Role of Data—Measuring What Matters.
Let’s take a closer look at why tracking the right things makes all the difference when it comes to making real progress.
You know, it’s pretty common to get caught up in measuring things like sales numbers, or chasing outside recognition. And sure, those results matter—but they’re often shaped by stuff you can’t completely control.
So, what if you shifted your focus to something that’s totally in your hands? Your own actions and daily habits.
Think of it like tending a garden. You can’t force a plant to grow, right? But you can water it, give it sunlight, and pull out the weeds. When you start tracking your own actions, you give yourself clarity—and you start to feel more in control.
So, how do you measure what really matters? Here are a few simple steps to get you started:
First, identify the actions you can actually control. Maybe it’s sticking to your daily routines or building those small habits.
Next, focus on tracking your inputs, not just the end result. For example, if you’re writing a book, record the number of pages you write each day—instead of just waiting for the moment you finish the whole thing.
Make it a habit to review your data. Look for patterns, celebrate your progress, and tweak your approach if you need to.
And finally, don’t get distracted by vanity metrics. Those shiny numbers that look impressive but don’t really reflect the effort you’re putting in? Let them go.
Picture this: someone learning to play guitar. Instead of counting the number of songs they’ve mastered, they track how many practice sessions they complete. Over time, those small, consistent actions build real skill—and before long, they’re playing songs with ease.
Here’s the real takeaway. When you measure what you can control, you’ll feel less anxious and a whole lot more motivated. The data you collect becomes your proof that progress is happening—even if the big results take a little while to show up.
